newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Manila shares likely to drop more.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Manila shares likely to drop more.

text.p: Manila shares on Wednesday gave up the resounding gains of the past two days and analysts said further falls were possible in what is certain to remain a very volatile market.

"This is a difficult call. It's tempting to say the market will continue to fall but some selloffs could have been overdone and so we could see some bargain hunting tommorrow. What's certain is the market will remain volatile," said one trader from a big foreign securities firm.
"The volatility is there. The past days run-up were technical and we still would shed more," said John Zarate, investment analyst at Vickers Ballas Securities Phils Inc.
The Philippines' main stock market index fell 82.13 points, or nearly three percent, ending at 2,694.40.
The market's barometer had surged by 170.88 points to 2,776.53 on Tuesday, a near seven percent rise in just two days from Friday's 2,605,65 and a correction was due, traders said.
Blue chip issues which had emerged victors since Monday came down with a thud on bouts of profit-taking.
Analysts said overall the market remained bearish as concern over an overheated property sector remained.

"The same fears are being conveniently resurrected. The principal culprit of the day is still that of the Thailand problem. I don't think the Philippines will join the funeral," said Joey Salceda, director at SBC Warburg.
Thai stocks were battered by the lunchbreak on Wednesday after opening at a 5-1/2 year low on renewed concern over problem loans in the property sector among other factors.
Fears of the Philippines following Thailand's path have been hounding the local equities market in the past few weeks.

Analysts said foreign investors, who were mostly on the sidelines during the two-day runup on Monday and Tuesday, would continue to remain cautious ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on May 20.
"Fed rates have always affected emerging markets and probably will continue to catch the eye of investors," said Vickers Ballas' Zarate.
"We will also go back to Dow watching to determine how the market will move," said Poch Zamora, dealer at Peregrine Securities.
Last week, the 2,600 level proved to be a strong support and analysts said the market may be headed for this psychological barrier if the main index dipped any further.

"We were faced with a seemingly bottomless pit about a week ago. We threw a stone into that pit and it echoed back saying we will test the 2,600 level. We will probably do so in the coming days," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities.
